question:
A 3-year-old male presents with a 4-week history of generalized fatigue and malaise. His medical
history includes full-term birth with no significant issues, and his mother has a history of recurring
anemia. Physical examination reveals pallor, jaundice, pale conjunctivae, and a spleen palpable 3–4
cm below the left costal margin. His vital signs show a temperature of 37°C (98.6°F) and pulse of
94/min. Laboratory findings are as follows: | Hemoglobin | 9.3 g/dL | | --- | --- | | Mean corpuscular
volume | 81.3 μm3 | | Mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration | 39% Hb/cell | | Leukocyte count |
7300/mm3 | | Platelet count | 200,000/mm3 | | Red cell distribution width | 19% (N = 13–15) | Which
diagnostic test would be most appropriate to confirm the suspected diagnosis? Answer Choices: (A)
Serum haptoglobin level (B) Genetic testing for alpha-thalassemia (C) Iron studies (D) Bone marrow
biopsy (E) Hemoglobin electrophoresis (F) Peripheral blood smear (G) Direct antiglobulin (Coombs)
test (H) Osmotic fragility test (I) Eosin-5-maleimide binding test (J) Reticulocyte count
 A. Osmotic fragility test
B. Peripheral blood smear
C. Iron studies
D. Eosin-5-maleimide binding test
E. Reticulocyte count
F. Serum haptoglobin level
G. Hemoglobin electrophoresis
H. Genetic testing for alpha-thalassemia
I. Direct antiglobulin (Coombs) test
J. Bone marrow biopsy
